name: Angular Leaf Spot of Cucumber
description: A bacterial disease causing angular water-soaked lesions on cucumber leaves. It is favored by cool, wet conditions and can cause significant defoliation and fruit spotting.
symptoms: Angular water-soaked lesions on leaves, delimited by veins
Lesions turning tan to brown with age
White bacterial exudate on lesion undersides in wet weather
Lesions drying and falling out, leaving shot-hole appearance
Small water-soaked spots on fruit turning white and cracking
causes: Seed-borne bacteria serving as primary inoculum
Rain splash and overhead irrigation spreading bacteria
High humidity and free moisture on leaves
treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides at first symptoms
Apply streptomycin where registered and available
prevention: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 30 min) before planting
Practice crop rotation with non-cucurbit crops
Avoid working in fields when leaves are wet
Space plants for good air circulation
